name: GO Classes GATE CS | Compiler Design | Syntax Directed Translation & SDD | Weekly Quiz 4

question.text:
Consider the following Syntax-Directed Definition $\text{(SDD)}$ for a simple desk calculator:
$$\begin{array}{|cl|l|}
\hline
& \text{PRODUCTION} & \text{SEMANTIC RULES} \\
\hline
1. & L \to E\ \textbf{n} & L.val = E.val \\
2. & E \to E_1 + T & E.val = E_1.val + T.val \\
3. & E \to T & E.val = T.val \\
4. & T \to T_1 * F & T.val = T_1.val \times F.val \\
5. & T \to F & T.val = F.val \\
6. & F \to (E) & F.val = E.val \\
7. & F \to \textbf{digit} & F.val = \textbf{digit}.lexval \\
   \hline
   \end{array}$$
An annotated parse tree is constructed and evaluated bottom-up for the input string $\verb|(9 + 8 * (7 + 6) + 5) * 4 n|$. What is the final evaluated value of the attribute $L.val$ at the root of the parse tree?

Consider the following Syntax-Directed Definition $\text{(SDD)}$ for a simple desk calculator:
$$\begin{array}{|cl|l|}
\hline
& \text{PRODUCTION} & \text{SEMANTIC RULES} \\
\hline
1. & L \to E\ \textbf{n} & L.val = E.val \\
2. & E \to E_1 + T & E.val = E_1.val + T.val \\
3. & E \to T & E.val = T.val \\
4. & T \to T_1 * F & T.val = T_1.val \times F.val \\
5. & T \to F & T.val = F.val \\
6. & F \to (E) & F.val = E.val \\
7. & F \to \textbf{digit} & F.val = \textbf{digit}.lexval\\
\hline
   \end{array}$$
An annotated parse tree is constructed and evaluated bottom-up for the input string $\verb|1 * (2 + 3) * 4 n|$. What is the final evaluated value of the attribute $L.val$ at the root of the parse tree?

Consider the following Syntax-Directed Translation Scheme $(SDTS)$:
$$\begin{array}{|ll|}
\hline
\textbf{SDT Scheme} \\
\hline
E \to E + T & \{\text{print } '+'\} \\
E \to E - T & \{\text{print } '-'\} \\
E \to T \\
T \to 0 & \{\text{print } '0'\} \\
T \to 1 & \{\text{print } '1'\} \\
\vdots \\
T \to 9 & \{\text{print } '9'\} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$
If this $\text{SDTS}$ is used to parse the input string $\verb|1 + 3 - 9 + 5 + 6 - 7 - 4|$, what will be the printed output?

  1. $\verb|+ - + + - - 1 3 9 5 6 7 4|$
     
  2. $\verb|1 3 + 9 - 5 + 6 + 7 - 4 -|$
     
  3. $\verb|1 3 9 5 6 7 4 + - + + - -|$
     
  4. $\verb|1 3 + 9 5 - + 6 7 - + 4 -|$

Consider the syntax directed translation scheme $\textsf{(SDTS)}$ given in the following. Assume attribute evaluation with bottom-up parsing, i.e., attributes are evaluated immediately after a reduction.

  • $E\rightarrow  E_{1} * T \qquad \{E.val = E_{1}.val * T.val\}$
  • $E\rightarrow  T \qquad \qquad \{E.val = T.val\}$
  • $T\rightarrow  F - T_{1}\qquad \{T.val = F.val - T_{1}.val\}$
  • $T\rightarrow F \qquad \qquad \{T.val = F.val\}$
  • $F\rightarrow 2 \qquad \qquad \{F.val = 2\}$
  • $F\rightarrow 4 \qquad \qquad \{F.val = 4\}$

Using this $\textsf{SDTS},$ for the expression $4 - 2 - 4 * 2$, what will be the $E.val$ ?

A. 12

B. 10

C. -6

D. -4

In the context of syntax-directed definitions $\text{(SDD)}$, consider a parse-tree node $N$ representing a nonterminal. Which of the following statements correctly identifies the dependencies of synthesized and inherited attributes at node $N$?

  1. A synthesized attribute at node $N$ is defined only in terms of attribute values at the children of $N$.
  2. An inherited attribute at node $N$ is defined only in terms of attribute values at $N's$ parent, $N$ itself, and $N's$ left siblings.
  3. An inherited attribute at node $N$ is defined only in terms of attribute values at $N's$ parent, $N$ itself, and $N's$ siblings.
  4. A synthesized attribute for a nonterminal $A$ at a parse-tree node $N$ is defined by a semantic rule associated with the production at a child of $N$.

Suppose that we have a production $A \to BCD$. Each of the four nonterminals $A, B, C,$ and $D$ has two attributes: $s$ is a synthesized attribute, and $i$ is an inherited attribute.

Consider the following two sets of semantic rules associated with this production:

  •  $\textbf{Set (a)}:A.s = B.i + C.s$
     
  •  $\textbf{Set (b)}:A.s = B.i + C.s\quad$ and $\quad D.i = A.i + B.s$

Which of the following statements is correct ?

  1. Both $\text{Set (a)}$ and $\text{Set (b)}$ are consistent with an S-attributed definition.
  2. Neither $\text{Set (a)}$ nor $\text{Set (b)}$ are consistent with an S-attributed definition.
  3. $\text{Set (a)}$ is consistent with an S-attributed definition, but $\text{Set (b)}$ is not.
  4. $\text{Set (b)}$ is consistent with an S-attributed definition, but $\text{Set (a)}$ is not.

Consider the following Syntax-Directed Definition $\text{(SDD)}$ based on a grammar suitable for top-down parsing:
$$\begin{array}{|cl|l|}
\hline
& \text{PRODUCTION} & \text{SEMANTIC RULES} \\
\hline
1. & T \to F\ T' & T'.inh = F.val \\
   &             & T.val = T'.syn \\
   
2. & T' \to *\ F\ T_1' & T_1'.inh = T'.inh \times F.val \\
   &                   & T'.syn = T_1'.syn \\
   
3. & T' \to \epsilon & T'.syn = T'.inh \\
 
4. & F \to \textbf{digit} & F.val = \textbf{digit}.lexval \\
   \hline
   \end{array}$$
In this $\text{SDD}$, nonterminals $T$ and $F$ have a synthesized attribute $val$. The terminal $\textbf{digit}$ has a synthesized attribute $lexval$. The nonterminal $T'$ has an inherited attribute $inh$ and a synthesized attribute $syn$.
For the input string $\verb|3 * 5|$, an annotated parse tree is constructed. What is the evaluated value of the attribute $T.val$ at the root of the parse tree?

Consider the following Syntax-Directed Translation $\text{(SDT)}$ scheme, where semantic actions contain print statements:
$$A \to A~\{\verb|print 'a'|\}~B \mid AB~\{\verb|print 'b'|\} \mid \verb|0|$$$$B \to B~\{\verb|print 'c'|\}~A \mid BA~\{\verb|print 'd'|\} \mid \verb|1|$$ If this $\text{SDT}$ is used to parse the input string $\verb|01001011|$, what will be the resulting printed output sequence?

  1. $\verb|a c a c b d a b|$
     
  2. $\verb|b d c a b d c a|$
     
  3. $\verb|a a b c c d a b|$
     
  4. The printed output cannot be uniquely determined because the grammar is ambiguous and contains syntactically identical productions with conflicting semantic actions.

Suppose that we have a production $A \to BCD$. Each of the four nonterminals $A, B, C,$ and $D$ has two attributes: $s$ is a synthesized attribute, and $i$ is an inherited attribute.

Consider the following two sets of semantic rules associated with this production:

  • $\textbf{Set (a)}: A.s = B.s + D.s$
     
  • $\textbf{Set (b)}: A.s = D.i,\quad B.i = A.s + C.s,\quad C.i = B.s,\quad \text{and}\quad D.i = B.i + C.i$

Which of the following statements is correct ?

A. Both $\text{Set (a)}$ and $\text{Set (b)}$ are consistent with an L-attributed definition.

B. Neither $\text{Set (a)}$ nor $\text{Set (b)}$ are consistent with an L-attributed definition.

C. $\text{Set (a)}$ is consistent with an L-attributed definition, but $\text{Set (b)}$ is not.

D. $\text{Set (b)}$ is consistent with an L-attributed definition, but $\text{Set (a)}$ is not.
